posts.title: Structuring a C++ Application - `main()` is an architecture decision
posts.description: Why C++ applications grow god classes, and how to structure one instead. Components with a lifecycle, a composition root in main(), and dependencies declared as types that the compiler checks, so the init and shutdown order is derived for you. Introduces keel, a single-header C++20 library built on these ideas.

posts.title: C++ will be safe one day, but it will be too late
posts.description: C++ will eventually gain safer features, but Rust’s memory safety model is already here; and flourishing. In this article, we explore why C++ might arrive too late to the safe-by-default party, despite its vast legacy ecosystem.

posts.title: Programming in C++ is hard, Software Engineering in C++ is even harder
posts.description: It is natural to assume that proficiency in C++ directly translates to the ability to develop software in the language. However, the two are not always synonymous. The complexities of C++ pose challenges for software engineering. Simplicity is important for maintainability and long-term success in software engineering.
